summary:
On January 8, 2024, at 12:45, Liberty County EMS Rescue 14 was dispatched to the NSK plant for an industrial machinery entrapment. The patient, Jonathan Davis, then 28, was found with his left arm crushed by a metal stamping press. A factory responder applied a tourniquet, EMS administered IV Fentanyl 100mcg, and he was transported to Midwest Regional Medical Center. He arrived at ED triage at 13:28 as ESI Level 1 (Emergent) with BP 88/50, HR 130, RR 24, SpO2 93%, and pain 10/10, and was admitted emergently to ICU-04 at 13:25 with a diagnosis of complete traumatic amputation between the shoulder and elbow, left arm (S48.112A), under attending Dr. Marcus Vance and admitting physician Dr. David Cho.

Diagnostic workup included X-ray and CT angiography showing extensive comminuted open segmental fractures of the forearm and hand, a comminuted displaced supracondylar humerus fracture, and complete cessation of contrast enhancement in the brachial artery at the distal third of the humerus, consistent with an unsalvageable limb. The emergency physician's impression was a mangled, unsalvageable left upper extremity with complete vascular and neurologic disruption and traumatic shock from acute blood loss. Labs showed leukocytosis (WBC 14.2) and anemia (Hgb 8.9, Hct 27.2); urine drug screen was positive for trace cannabinoids and negative for ethanol.

After transfusion of 2 units PRBC, the patient underwent emergent left transhumeral (above-elbow) amputation by Dr. Vance, with myofascial closure, bone beveling, and traction-neurectomy of the median, ulnar, and radial nerves; EBL was 650 mL and a JP drain was placed. Postoperative pain management included a Dilaudid PCA, Gabapentin 300mg, Ancef 1g IV, and PRN Oxycodone 5–10mg. The JP drain was removed on postoperative day 4 (January 12), and he was discharged January 15 after a 7-day admission on Gabapentin 300mg TID, Oxycodone 5mg q4-6h PRN, and Cefdinir 300mg BID for 5 days, with follow-up arranged with Dr. Vance and PM&R/prosthetic evaluation with Dr. Elena Rostova.

By the one-month follow-up (February 12, 2024), the stump had healed but severe phantom limb pain (8/10) and stump hypersensitivity prompted increasing Gabapentin to 600mg TID and referrals for desensitization therapy and shrinker sock fitting. At five months (June 18, 2024), a tender 1.5cm mobile nodule was identified as a traumatic neuroma of the ulnar/median nerve stump, interfering with prosthetic fitting; excision (1.8 x 1.4 cm) with nerve transposition and embedding into the triceps was performed by Dr. Vance on November 12, 2024.

In December 2024, Liberty Mutual placed prosthetic therapy authorization on hold pending peer review of the proposed myoelectric prosthesis, suspending PT/OT. Rehabilitation resumed January 2025, with a myoelectric transhumeral prosthesis (carbon-fiber socket, Utah Myoelectric Elbow, Motion Control MC Hand) fitted February 5, 2025, achieving 80% electrode signal accuracy. Ten PT visits followed through June 2026, with pain declining from 5/10 to 1/10, interrupted by two no-shows (May 12 and November 10, 2025). At discharge (June 22, 2026), the patient had achieved master-level prosthesis operation, independent ADLs, driving, carrying up to 25 lbs, near-normal shoulder ROM, and clearance to modified light/medium duty at NSK.
